chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not grant people absolute freedom in their actions, but He gave them a choice between obedience and disobedience.
So whoever obeys Him enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys Him enters Hellfire.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic view on human free will and predestination?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the position between the two positions), affirming that divine decree does not negate human agency. This nuanced view rejects both the absolute predestination of the Qadariyyah and the total compulsion attributed to the Jabriyyah, establishing a balanced framework where humans are accountable for their voluntary choices.
